thread.title: GOP Approves New Map in Missouri - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: GOP Approves New Map in Missouri - NewsBreak

author: Roger Anderson
title: GOP Approves New Map in Missouri - NewsBreak
text:
By Roger Anderson ,
5 hours ago Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe and Republican lawmakers have approved a new congressional map intended to boost Republican representation. The NAACP and ACLU of Missouri have criticized the map for potential constitutional and racial bias. In response, the group People NOT Politicians has begun collecting roughly 110,000 signatures to suspend the map and submit it to a statewide vote.
Rep. Emanuel Cleaver (D-MO) said, “I think the people around the country are supporting the people in Missouri who are ready to go.” Cleaver added, “I didn’t knock on doors and get signatures, and it is my belief they’ll have the signatures needed to put this on the ballot.”
Kehoe said, “I was proud to officially sign the Missouri First Map into law today ahead of the 2026 midterm election.”
Kehoe added, “We believe this map best represents Missourians, and I appreciate the support and efforts of state legislators, our congressional delegation, and President Trump in getting this map to my desk.”
The legislature has prompted lawsuits alleging procedural, racial, and authority concerns over the extraordinary session. The NAACP and ACLU of Missouri argued the process lacked authority and that some districts may disproportionately affect minority voters.
Republicans have defended the map, citing legislative authority. Kehoe stated, “We’ll let the courts decide on that.”
Kehoe added, “I’m comfortable with the folks that we’ve been working with. I really believe they’re very good on these issues, and we think we’ll withstand all those challenges.”
Roger Anderson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
